mechanism: Selective T cell costimulation modulator (label wording)
route: Intravenous infusion at launch; subcutaneous injection added 2011-07-29
dosing: IV: weight-based 500 mg / 750 mg / 1,000 mg at weeks 0, 2 and 4, then every 4 weeks; SC: 125 mg once weekly (2023 label)
first_us_indication: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adults with an inadequate response to one or more DMARDs such as methotrexate or TNF antagonists
other_us_indications: moderate to severe polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (intravenous) 2008-04-07; polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis age 2+ (subcutaneous regimen) 2017-03-30; psoriatic arthritis 2017-06-30; prophylaxis of acute graft versus host disease with a calcineurin inhibitor and methotrexate (HSCT from a matched or 1 allele-mismatched unrelated donor; age 2+) 2021-12-15; active psoriatic arthritis age 2+ (subcutaneous) 2023-10-30
notes: Approval date: the text layer of the scanned original letter has no legible date; FDA S-240 letter states "Orencia (abatacept) was approved on December 23, 2005" (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/125118Orig1s240ltr.pdf) and openFDA Drugs@FDA lists BLA 125118 original approval 2005-12-23. Supplement dates are openFDA submission status dates; indications from FDA letters S-045 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2008/125118s045ltr.pdf, stamped APR 7 2008), S-211 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/125118Orig1s211ltr.pdf), S-209 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2017/125118Orig1s209ltr.pdf, signed 06/30/2017), S-240 (signed 12/15/2021), S-250 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2023/125118Orig1s250ltr.pdf, signed 10/30/2023). Subcutaneous use for RA: S-122 letter dated July 29, 2011 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2011/125118s0122ltr.pdf); removal of IV loading dose for SC: S-171, 2013-12-20. No UC or CD approval found. US launch in February 2006 per BMS Q1 2006 release; the Q4 2005 release prints no Orencia sales. BMS was the only reporting company in the window, and Orencia is still a BMS product line in the 2020-2026 releases read.

company_at_launch: Bristol Myers Squibb (NDA held by its subsidiary Celgene)
dosing: Oral, 0.92 mg once daily from day 8 after a 7-day titration (0.23 mg days 1-4, 0.46 mg days 5-7)
first_us_indication: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults (clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease and active secondary progressive disease)
notes: Original NDA letter addressed to Celgene Corporation, e-signed 03/25/2020. UC (moderately to severely active, adults): S-001 letter e-signed 05/27/2021 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2021/209899Orig1s001ltr.pdf). No Crohn's disease approval among the efficacy supplements listed by openFDA Drugs@FDA (data updated 2026-11-17). BMS completed its acquisition of Celgene on 2019-11-20 (BMS 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/14272/000114036119021048/form8k.htm), before launch, so BMS has recorded all Zeposia sales. BMS Q2 2020 release: US commercial launch announced in June 2020; the Q1 2020 release prints no Zeposia revenue.
